Description

In the mast cell, cytosolic phospholipase A2 releases arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids. Cyclooxygenases 1 and 2 turn it into the prostaglandin endoperoxides PGG2 and PGH2, from which specific synthases make PGE2, PGD2, PGF2alpha, PGI2 and thromboxane A2. The lipoxygenases ALOX5, ALOX12 and ALOX15 make the hydroperoxy and hydroxy acids, the leukotrienes (LTB4 and the cysteinyl leukotrienes LTC4, LTD4, LTE4), lipoxins, eoxins and hepoxilins. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and paracetamol inhibit the cyclooxygenase step, and corticosteroids reduce the release of arachidonic acid. PGE2, PGI2 and LTB4 leave the cell and act on the receptors of the nociceptor.
